messages.author: b7eb8dffd6e11039
messages.subject: Using color for two aesthetics
parts:
Suppose I have a data frame df_poly that specifies the polygons for
the counties of Iowa and Illinois. My data frame has a variable State
which specifies what state each polygon belongs to. For each county I
have a variable X which I want to use as fill color. I have another
data frame df_points with lat/long and a factor Y which has two levels
(a,b).

I would like to plot a map where the border color of the counties is
specified by State (e.g. all the Iowa counties have green borders and
the Illinois counties have orange borders). I would like the fill to
be specified by X. And I would like the points to be colored by Y. I
used:

ggplot(df_poly,aes(long,lat)) +
geom_polygon(aes(group=group,fill=X,color=S)) +
geom_point(data=df_points,aes(color=Y))

The problem is that the legend is collapsing the colors for S and Y
into a single legend. So for the legend I have:

State
illinois
iowa
a
b

X
100
200
300

I would like to have:

State
illinois
iowa

Y
a
b

X
100
200
300

Is there a way to do this?

messages.author: 99a1cfc66539313c
messages.subject: Re: Using color for two aesthetics
parts:
Dave

It is always easier to reply to questions if you post a minimal,
reproducible example.

However, I have created an example that illustrates what I think you
mean. I create two data.frames, one with circles and the second with
squares. I map the circle colour to colour, and I map the square
colour to fill. I then create a scale for colour and a scale for
fill.

Note that nothing gets mapped in the basic call to ggplot(). All of
the data and aesthetic mapping happens in the geoms.

Andrie

library(ggplot2)
circles <- data.frame(
x=runif(20,0,10),
y=runif(20,0,10),
r=runif(20,1,3),
cfill=rnorm(20,5,2))

squares <- data.frame(
x=runif(20,0,10),
y=runif(20,0,10),
w=runif(20,0.1,0.5),
sfill=rnorm(20,10,2))

g <- ggplot() +
geom_point(data=circles,
aes(x=x, y=y, size=r, colour=cfill)) +
scale_colour_gradient("circle") +
geom_rect(data=squares,
aes(xmin=x, ymin=y, xmax=x+w, ymax=y+w, fill=sfill))
+
scale_fill_gradient("square")

print(g)

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Using color for two aesthetics
parts:
Hi:

This is nice! The only concern I have is that the colors of the points can be overshadowed by those of the states. The easiest fix for that is to lower the alpha transparency. One still has the option to use shapes for points, or perhaps a combination of shapes and colors. Here are a couple of examples, extending slightly what Brandon has taken far.

# More dramatic point colors to offset the tinted state backgrounds, with lower alpha transparency:
g + geom_polygon(aes(fill=region, group=group), alpha=0.1) +
    geom_path(aes(group=group))+
    geom_point(data=df_points,aes(color=y))+
    scale_color_manual(values = c('red', 'blue'))

# Different point shapes with colors, extending the above:
g + geom_polygon(aes(fill=region, group=group), alpha=0.1) +
    geom_path(aes(group=group))+
    geom_point(data=df_points,aes(shape=y, color = y), size = 3) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c('red', 'blue'))

One could also dispense with the colors and go with the shapes, perhaps saving colors for a different aesthetic.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: Using color for two aesthetics
parts:
Shown?

df_poly<-map_data("county",c("missouri"))

df_points <- data.frame(
long=runif(5,min(df_poly$long),max(df_poly$long)),
lat=runif(5,min(df_poly$lat),max(df_poly$lat)),
y=c("A","B","B","A","B"))

ggplot(df_poly,aes(long,lat)) +
geom_polygon(aes(fill=region, group=group), alpha=0.35) +

geom_path(aes(group=group))+
geom_point(data=df_points,aes(shape=y, color = y), size = 3)+

scale_color_manual(values = c('red', 'blue'))+
theme_bw()+
opts(title="Missouri: Most Important State in the Union")

Defining the colors and increasing the point size was definitely an improvement. Also, I think if you take out the background and increase the alpha a bit (0.1->0.35) the whole thing looks a bit better. Especially with the location change. 

Brandon
